title: INT8 weight-only: hardware-adaptive calibration & telemetry-driven smoke suite
creator: Jia Chen
description:
Objective: integrate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles into the main CI and nightly regression suite with hardware-adaptive calibration and telemetry-driven smoke tests. The goal is to ensure we ship weight-only INT8 profiles that are validated against accuracy guardrails and behave predictably across target GPU families (A100, H100, RTX 6000, and a CPU fallback path).

Scope: This ticket covers: (1) authoring a calibration orchestration that picks quantization profile variants per hardware family, (2) extending the nightly calibration runner to produce a per-profile accuracy delta report, (3) adding telemetry hooks for per-model-token log-likelihood drift and throughput delta, and (4) a small smoke acceptance suite that gates canary deploys of weight-only INT8 profiles.

Why this is needed: Previous field incidents showed regressions when a profile tuned on A100 kernels was applied to H100 or mixed GPU clusters. We need a repeatable, automated process that identifies hardware-specific regressions early, triggers canary rollouts only when within tolerances, and provides clear signals (LL-delta, top-1 token regression rate, and latency p99) for rollback automation.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly calibration runner produces accuracy_delta artifacts for every new weight-only INT8 profile (GPTQ/AWQ) and stores them in s3://redwood-quant/profiles/<profile>/<date>/accuracy.json
CI job 'int8-wo-hw-smoke' runs on PRs that touch quantization code and fails if LL-delta > 1.5% or token-regression-rate > 0.7% on the golden prompt set
Hardware-adaptive selection logic (profile -> kernel mapping) implemented and covered by unit tests for A100/H100/RTX/CPU paths
Telemetry events emitted with model, profile_id, kernel_family, ll_delta, p99_latency, and tokens_served and visible in Console dashboard
Canary rollout pipeline can be triggered with the smoke suite and will auto-block if accuracy regressions exceed thresholds
tasks: Design profile metadata extension (profile.yaml) to include hardware_affinity and fallback_order
Implement profile selector service changes to pick kernel_family at runtime based on node labels
Add telemetry emissions in inference runtime for profile validation metrics
Create 'int8-wo-hw-smoke' GH Action and CI pipeline step with a small golden prompt set
Integrate nightly calibration runner with regression reporter and S3 sink
Author canary playbook: thresholds, rollback steps, monitoring links
comments: 2025-01-10 - Jia Chen: Spike completed. Verified GPTQ profiles tuned on A100 show ~0.9% LL-delta vs FP16 on our conv simple-eval set, but the same profile on H100 shows spikes up to 2.2% — suggests kernel numerics differences. Next: capture per-layer quant stats in calibration artifacts.

2025-01-13 - Marco Fernández: Implemented profile metadata change and a prototype selector. Submitted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128 (do not merge). Needs tests for mixed-cluster labeling.

2025-01-15 - Quant Team review (notes): Agree on hardware_affinity field. Recommend naming: 'preferred_kernels' + 'fallback_kernels'. Also add 'calibration_seed' to profile so nightly runs are reproducible.

2025-01-17 - Marco Fernández: Telemetry schema proposal posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/quant/telemetry-int8. Schema includes ll_delta, token_regression_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_family. Sync scheduled with Observability on 2025-01-20.

2025-01-21 - Observability: Confirmed we can ingest events at needed cardinality. Added retention note: 90 days for per-profile aggregates. Linked dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-dashboards/pull/78
notes: Fallback behavior: if token-level latency exceeds 2x baseline or p99 latency breaches configured SLO, the selector will prefer a higher-precision kernel (FP16) for that request class. We will also add a lightweight fuzz test in CI that asserts no NaNs/infs are produced by the quantized kernels. Nightly regression will run with a seeded RNG to improve flakiness detection.
